physiology:
The traditions seat this code in the small folded structure deep in the brain that holds memory, the hippocampus, and in the wider quiet machinery around it where the day gets sorted into what stays and what falls away. It is the part of you that decides, while you sleep, which hours from the last waking stretch are worth keeping. It is fitting. This is the code of retreat and remembering, and the body's own retreat is the night, when this small organ goes through the harvest the keys section asked you to make on purpose.

The shadow has its bodily floor here. When the days are run through at speed and nothing is stopped for, the hippocampus has almost nothing to file. The week thins. Whole afternoons fail to leave a trace, not because the mind chose to forget, but because the body was never given the pause it needs to lay anything down. Long stretches of this register as a kind of fog behind the eyes, a tiredness that sleep does not fully clear.

The climb out is also bodily, and it is quieter than people expect. A slow cup of tea, an unhurried meal, a sit-down in the middle of the day with no screen in it, and the small organ at the back of the brain begins to do what it was always trying to do. The hours start to settle. The good ones get kept. By evening you can feel where the day actually went. The remembering is metabolic before it is anything else.
amino_acid:
Deeper than the organ, this code answers to no amino acid at all. In the language of the genetic code there are three stop codons, the punctuation marks that tell the cell the sentence is finished and to let the protein go. This card is one of them. Where the other sixty-three codes build a letter into the body's chemistry, this one writes the silence after.

There is a teaching in that, and it is the quiet one at the centre of this card. The forgetting is what happens when a life is run as one long unbroken sentence, no pause, no stop, no breath. The body cannot harvest what it cannot finish. The chemistry says the same thing the gift says, lower down than any practice. The pause is not the absence of the code. The pause is the code. When the day is finally allowed to come to a rest, the small organ in the back of the brain takes the harvest the stop made possible, and what was lived becomes, at last, remembered.
